preamble: Pulmonary Valve Disease and RVOT Obstruction  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  ACC/AHA 2018 CHD Guidelines / AHA/ACC 2022 Valve Guidelines / Repaired TOF Long-Term Outcome Data  |  RV Dysfunction and Intervention Risk Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is RVEDVi >150 mL/m² or RVESVi >80 mL/m² on cardiac MRI?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe RV dilation confirmed; RVEDVi >150 mL/m² is the most validated CMR threshold for pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in repaired TOF; PVR at this threshold achieves best RV reverse remodeling

questions.question: Is RVEF <45% on CMR (RV systolic dysfunction from chronic volume or pressure overload)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — RVEF <45% confirmed; independent criterion for PVR timing; RVEF <40% predicts irreversible dysfunction if intervention delayed; urgent referral for TPVR or surgical PVR

questions.question: Is there severe pulmonary regurgitation (PR fraction >40% on CMR or dense PR jet on echo without end-diastolic flow reversal)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe PR confirmed; primary driver of progressive RV dilation in repaired TOF and post-valvotomy; PR fraction >40% is a Class I CMR indication for PVR timing assessment

questions.question: Is peak pulmonary valve gradient >64 mmHg (peak Doppler velocity >4.0 m/s) or peak RV–PA gradient >40 mmHg on cath?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe PS confirmed; Class I indication for intervention (BPV or surgical/transcatheter PVR); RV pressure >2/3 systemic is an independent high-risk marker

questions.question: Is there significant combined pulmonary stenosis and regurgitation (gradient >36 mmHg + PR fraction >25%)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — mixed PS/PR lesion confirmed; double burden on RV; often seen in repaired TOF with RVOT patch; accelerates RV dilation and dysfunction

questions.question: Is there documented sustained ventricular tachycardia, resuscitated cardiac arrest, or unexplained syncope in the setting of RVOT disease?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — ventricular arrhythmia or SCA confirmed; major SCD risk marker in repaired TOF; ICD implantation indicated; electrophysiology study and ablation considered; urgent PVR to reduce arrhythmia substrate

questions.question: Is QRS duration ≥180 ms on 12-lead ECG (in repaired TOF or other RVOT surgery)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — QRS ≥180 ms confirmed; strongest ECG predictor of SCD in repaired TOF; combined with RV dilation, marks highest arrhythmia risk subgroup; PVR shortens QRS and reduces SCD risk

questions.question: Is there exertional dyspnea, exercise intolerance (≥2 MET limitation), or new-onset right heart failure (peripheral edema, hepatomegaly, ascites)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — symptomatic RV decompensation confirmed; primary clinical driver of intervention; NYHA class II–IV in RVOT disease indicates RV reserve exhaustion; intervention urgency elevated

questions.question: Does cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) show VO₂ max <65% predicted or VE/VCO₂ slope >34?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — objectively reduced exercise capacity confirmed; reflects chronotropic incompetence or reduced RV stroke volume augmentation; supports intervention even in borderline-symptomatic patients

questions.question: Is there a history of surgical repair of Tetralogy of Fallot (complete repair with transannular patch or conduit)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — repaired TOF confirmed; most common indication for PVR in adolescents and adults; transannular patch repair causes free PR; conduit repair causes mixed PS/PR; lifelong cardiology follow-up mandatory

questions.question: Is there Noonan syndrome (PTPN11/SOS1/RAF1) or other syndrome (Williams, Alagille, CHARGE) as the underlying etiology of RVOT disease?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — syndromic RVOT disease confirmed; Noonan PS typically dysplastic — responds poorly to BPV; surgical valvotomy or PVR preferred; syndrome-specific cardiovascular surveillance required

questions.question: Is the conduit or native RVOT diameter 16–30 mm and is coronary compression testing negative, confirming TPVR candidacy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — TPVR candidacy confirmed (Melody, SAPIEN 3, or Harmony TPV); transcatheter approach preferred over surgery in suitable anatomy; reduces procedural risk and recovery time vs. repeat open-heart surgery

questions.question: Is the existing RV-PA conduit calcified or obstructed in a pattern requiring bare-metal prestenting before TPVR?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — conduit calcification requiring prestenting confirmed; increases procedural complexity; prestenting optimizes landing zone and reduces conduit fracture risk post-TPVR
